**Evidence required for a duplicate‑payment refund** | Type of evidence | What to provide | Why it matters | |------------------|-----------------|----------------| | **Original payment confirmation** | • Bank/credit‑card statement showing the duplicate charge.
• Screenshot or PDF of the transaction record. | Confirms that the same amount was charged twice. | | **Merchant receipt / order confirmation** | • PDF or image of the receipt that lists the duplicated item(s).
• Order number, date, and item details. | Links the duplicate charge to a specific purchase. | | **Proof of delivery / service completion** | • Delivery confirmation (tracking number, signed delivery receipt).
• Service completion note or invoice. | Shows that the goods/services were actually received, supporting the claim that the duplicate payment was unnecessary. | | **Correspondence with merchant** | • Emails, chat logs, or letters where the merchant acknowledges the duplicate charge or agrees to refund. | Demonstrates that the merchant is aware of the issue and is willing to resolve it. | | **Account statement showing the refund** | • Bank statement or credit‑card statement showing the refund transaction (if already processed). | Confirms that the refund has been issued and the amount matches the duplicate payment. | | **Identity verification** | • Copy of a government‑issued ID or passport. | Ensures the claim is made by the rightful account holder. | | **Any additional supporting documents** | • For example, a signed authorization form, a signed receipt, or a signed refund request form. | Provides extra assurance that the duplicate payment was legitimate and that the refund is justified. | ### How to submit the evidence 1. **Gather all documents** in PDF or high‑resolution image format. 2. **Organize them** by type (payment confirmation, receipt, correspondence, etc.). 3. **Upload** the files through the platform’s dispute or refund portal, or attach them to an email to the merchant’s support address. 4. **Include a brief explanation** of why each document is relevant and how it supports the duplicate‑payment claim. ### Tips for a smooth refund process - **Keep copies** of everything you send. - **Label files clearly** (e.g., “DuplicatePayment_Statement.pdf”). - **Check the merchant’s refund policy** for any specific documentation requirements. - **Follow up** if you don’t receive a response within the merchant’s stated time frame (usually 7–14 business days). Providing complete, clear evidence will speed up the refund and reduce the likelihood of the claim being denied.

### Handling a Locked Account – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a concise, customer‑friendly workflow that covers everything from initial detection to final resolution. Feel free to adapt the wording to your brand voice, but keep the core steps intact. | # | Action | What to Say | Why It Matters | |---|--------|-------------|----------------| | 1 | **Verify Identity** | “I’m going to verify a few details to make sure we’re talking to the rightful owner.” | Prevents fraud and protects the customer’s data. | | 2 | **Explain the Lock Reason** | “Your account is currently locked because of X (e.g., multiple failed log‑ins, suspicious activity, or a policy violation).” | Transparency builds trust and sets expectations. | | 3 | **Offer Immediate Options** | • “We can unlock your account right now.”
• “Or we can walk through a reset to regain access.” | Gives the customer agency and speeds up resolution. | | 4 | **Perform the Unlock (if chosen)** | “I’m unlocking your account now. You should be able to log in shortly.” | Quick win – reduces friction. | | 5 | **Reset Password (if needed)** | “Let’s set a new password. Please choose a strong one that you haven’t used before.” | Reinforces security and prevents re‑locking. | | 6 | **Educate on Prevention** | “To avoid future locks, please… (e.g., enable 2FA, avoid using the same password across sites).” | Reduces repeat incidents and improves user experience. | | 7 | **Confirm Resolution** | “Can you try logging in now? Let me know if you see any issues.” | Ensures the problem is truly solved. | | 8 | **Close with Support Info** | “If you run into any more trouble, you can reach us at… or reply to this email.” | Keeps the line open for follow‑up. | --- ## Detailed Script (Optional) > **Agent:** Hi [Customer Name], I’m [Your Name] from the Support Team. I see your account is locked. I’ll need to verify a few details to keep your account safe. > **Customer:** Sure. > **Agent:** Great. Can you confirm the last four digits of your SSN (or the email address you used to register)? > **Customer:** 1234. > **Agent:** Thanks. Your account is locked because of [specific reason]. We can unlock it right now or reset your password. Which would you prefer? > **Customer:** Unlock, please. > **Agent:** I’m unlocking it now. You should be able to log in in the next minute. > **Customer:** I can log in. > **Agent:** Fantastic! To prevent this from happening again, I recommend enabling two‑factor authentication and using a unique password. > **Customer:** Will do. > **Agent:** If you need anything else, just reply to this email or call us at 1‑800‑XXX‑XXXX. Have a great day! --- ## Quick Reference Checklist - [ ] Verify identity (security question, email, phone, etc.) - [ ] Identify lock cause (policy, security, admin action) - [ ] Offer unlock or password reset - [ ] Execute chosen action - [ ] Educate on prevention (2FA, password hygiene) - [ ] Confirm login success - [ ] Provide next‑step contact info --- ### FAQ for Support Agents | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Can I unlock an account without a password reset?** | Yes, if the lock is due to failed log‑ins or policy, a simple unlock is fine. | | **What if the customer can’t remember their identity details?** | Offer alternate verification (e.g., last transaction, security code sent to phone). | | **When should I ask for a password reset instead of unlocking?** | If the lock was triggered by a suspected compromise or the password is weak. | | **Do I need to log the action?** | Yes – record the unlock, the reason, and any new password policy applied. | --- ### Final Tip **Keep the tone calm, concise, and reassuring.** Locked accounts can be stressful for customers; a quick, clear resolution will turn a potential frustration into a positive experience.

**Subject: Confirmation of Personal Data Deletion Request**

Dear [Customer Name],

Thank you for contacting us. We have received your request to delete all personal data associated with your account. We take privacy and data protection very seriously and will comply with your request in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

**Next Steps**

1. **Verification** – To confirm that this request is legitimate, please provide one of the following:
   - A copy of a government‑issued ID (e.g., driver’s license, passport) that matches the name on the account.
   - A recent utility bill or bank statement showing your name and address.
   - Any other official document that verifies your identity.

2. **Account Details** – Please confirm the email address or phone number associated with the account you wish to delete.

Once we receive the verification documents and account details, we will proceed with the deletion process. The deletion will be completed within **5 business days** from the date of verification.

**What Happens Next**

- All personal data stored in our systems (including but not limited to contact information, transaction history, and any other personal identifiers) will be permanently deleted.
- We will send you a confirmation email once the deletion is complete.
- If you have any questions or need assistance during this process, please reply to this email or call our support line at [Support Phone Number].

Thank you for your cooperation. We look forward to resolving this matter promptly.

Best regards,

[Your Name]  
Data Privacy Officer  
[Company Name]  
[Contact Information]

**Evidence required for a duplicate‑payment refund**

| Evidence Type | What to provide | Why it matters |
|---------------|-----------------|----------------|
| **Original payment confirmation** | A screenshot or PDF of the original transaction receipt (e‑mail, bank statement, or payment gateway confirmation) showing the amount, date, and merchant. | Confirms that the payment was actually made and establishes the amount to be refunded. |
| **Duplicate payment confirmation** | A separate receipt or screenshot that shows the same amount charged again on a different date or transaction ID. | Demonstrates that the same amount was charged twice. |
| **Merchant communication** | Any email, chat transcript, or letter from the merchant confirming that the duplicate charge was a mistake and that they will issue a refund. | Provides the merchant’s acknowledgment and intent to refund. |
| **Bank or card statement** | A copy of the statement that lists both charges and the refund (if already processed). | Offers an independent record of the transactions and the refund amount. |
| **Refund receipt** | If the refund has already been issued, a screenshot or PDF of the refund confirmation (date, amount, reference number). | Shows that the refund was completed and verifies the amount. |
| **Proof of identity (if required)** | A scanned ID or a selfie‑verification photo. | Ensures the request is coming from the rightful account holder. |

**How to submit**

1. **Gather all documents** – keep them in PDF or high‑resolution image format.  
2. **Upload** – use the “Upload Evidence” button in the duplicate‑payment refund request form.  
3. **Label clearly** – name each file (e.g., “Original_Receipt_2024-10-01.pdf”).  
4. **Confirm** – double‑check that the amounts match across all documents.

**What happens next**

- The support team will review the evidence.  
- If everything matches, the refund will be processed automatically.  
- If any evidence is missing or unclear, you’ll receive a request for additional information.

Providing all of the above evidence in one go speeds up the process and reduces back‑and‑forth communication.

**Evidence Required for a Duplicate‑Payment Refund (Request 10)** | Category | Specific Evidence | Why It’s Needed | How to Submit | |----------|-------------------|-----------------|---------------| | **Proof of Duplicate Charge** | • Bank or credit‑card statement showing the same transaction amount twice on the same date.
• Merchant receipt or invoice that lists the same item/service twice. | Confirms that the customer was charged twice for the same purchase. | Upload a clear PDF/scan or provide a screenshot (max 5 MB). | | **Customer Confirmation** | • Written statement (email, chat transcript, or signed letter) from the customer acknowledging the duplicate charge. | Establishes the customer’s claim and intent to request a refund. | Attach the email or chat export; if a letter, scan it. | | **Merchant Confirmation** | • Merchant’s internal transaction log or POS record showing two separate entries for the same order ID. | Validates that the duplicate charge originated from the merchant’s system, not a processing error. | Upload the log or a screenshot; if unavailable, a written confirmation from the merchant’s finance team. | | **Order/Invoice Details** | • Original order number, date, and item description. | Links the duplicate charge to a specific transaction. | Provide the invoice or order confirmation PDF. | | **Refund Request Form** | • Completed duplicate‑payment refund request form (if your platform requires one). | Standardizes the request and ensures all required fields are filled. | Fill out the form online or attach a PDF. | | **Payment Method Details** | • Last four digits of the card or account number used for the purchase. | Helps the payment processor locate the correct transaction. | Include in the request form or as a separate note. | | **Time‑Stamp Evidence** | • Time‑stamped screenshots of the merchant’s dashboard showing both charges. | Demonstrates that the duplicate occurred within the same transaction window. | Upload screenshots; ensure the timestamp is visible. | | **Optional: Transaction ID(s)** | • Unique transaction IDs for each charge. | Makes it easier to trace the payments in the payment gateway. | Provide in the request form or as a separate document. | ### Quick Checklist 1. **Duplicate Charge Proof** – statement or receipt. 2. **Customer Confirmation** – email/chat/letter. 3. **Merchant Confirmation** – transaction log or written statement. 4. **Order Details** – invoice or order confirmation. 5. **Refund Request Form** – if required. 6. **Payment Method** – last four digits. 7. **Time‑Stamp Evidence** – screenshots with timestamps. 8. **Transaction IDs** – optional but helpful. ### Submission Tips - **File Format:** PDF, PNG, or JPEG. - **File Size:** Keep each file under 5 MB; compress if necessary. - **Clarity:** Ensure all text is legible; blur sensitive data that isn’t needed. - **Order:** Attach files in the order listed above to avoid confusion. Providing all of the above evidence will expedite the duplicate‑payment refund process and reduce the likelihood of additional follow‑up requests.
